mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances with PAYEMS month-over-month increase, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% signals an overheating labor market that typically precedes Federal Reserve monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 5.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous exceedance of 12-month moving averages by nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals synchronized economic expansion that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS and HOUST both exceed 12-month moving averages, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), a strong labor market (PAYEMS > 145,000) signals an overheating economy that may trigger aggressive rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during FEDFUNDS > 4.0% with PAYEMS > 145,000, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 105.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals rising inflation that typically prompts Federal Reserve monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output that boosts corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances with INDPRO month-over-month increase, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above 560,000 million dollars signals strong consumer demand that typically drives corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances with RSAFS > 560,000, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
